Really, the only thing that kept me sane was good ol' vidya. Battlefield, Assassin's Creed, didn't really matter. It shut the world off for a time and that's all I could really do. There wasn't much in the way of fighting back.

I've observed something really interesting though, despite all this. I think I've reached a point where I'm kinda used to all this shit. Pain and whatnot.

Back in HS, I used to get a weird sinking feeling in my chest that hurt like Hell when reminding myself there wouldn't be anyone later, so stop fucking trying now. Anymore, it's really just a numb feeling. Just a... Hell I don't even know. It's like hitting a wall with a pillow I guess, and you're the wall. You feel it, but you don't feel it, if you catch my drift.

I think this because of all the "mental conditioning" I ran myself through. In the hopes of eventually numbing everything, I just repeatedly reminded myself of the reality of my situation. There would be nobody, I'm dying alone, just telling myself shit to fuck me up even worse.

Having done this though, it seems to have worked very well. Perhaps a little too well. It's quite difficult to display any emotion other than varying levels of anger. That's my sword and my shield though. The second I'm not pissed off, the gates are open and a world of shit comes about. Granted, I'm not constantly seething just waiting for a fight, most of the time you'd never really tell exactly what I'm doing. I'd seem more high-strung/tense than anything.

I could talk about this shit for hours and still not get it across the way I need to. It's just one of those things you need to experience to understand, in all reality. Sounds like a cop-out, but I really don't have any way to properly describe it all.

SO...

Tl;Dr: Too much straw breaks the animal's back.
